_meta.title: AI Acceptable Use — System Authorisation Record

step-2.business_case: JAKE is an AI assistant used by the Legal and Procurement teams to answer questions from uploaded customer contracts and draft summary clauses. It runs on a third-party foundation-model API; our organisation is the deployer. Its outputs are shared with clients. It processes customer contracts and financial records, which include personal data (PII). People use its outputs as the basis for decisions; human verification is currently informal. If it produces an incorrect or hallucinated output, the assessed business impact is severe, and could cause a regulatory or compliance breach.

step-3.rationale: High-risk: assists decisions affecting access to an essential service; deployer role; transparency and human-oversight obligations apply.

privacy_risks: Personal data egress to a third-party model

risks.risk_name: Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress

requirements.notes:
AI Governance Workflow — Compliance Strategy
This AI governance workflow (Steps 3–7 and the AI Act Compliance Controls view) constitutes the organisation's formal compliance strategy under ISO 18286.1, providing a repeatable, auditable process for identifying applicable obligations, treating risks, selecting controls, and maintaining ongoing HS traceability.

AI Governance Workflow — Accountability Framework
This AI governance workflow constitutes the organisation's accountability framework under ISO 18286.2, with defined roles and escalation paths from requestor through Department Head, AI Governance Team, DPO, AI Change Board, and CISO/Steering Committee.

AI Governance Workflow — Design and Development Controls
Steps 5 and 6 of the AI governance workflow, combined with the Step 8 Board gate and Step 7 controls verification, constitute the organisation's design and development control process under ISO 18286.3.

AI Governance Workflow — Resource Management
The AI governance workflow embeds resource management under ISO 18286.4 through mandatory competence prerequisites, specialist function assignments, and targeted user briefings at each stage.

AI Governance Workflow — Post-Market Monitoring
Step 12 of the AI governance workflow constitutes the organisation's post-market monitoring system under ISO 18286.5, providing risk-proportionate periodic reviews and event-triggered re-assessments across the full lifecycle of each approved AI use case.

AI Governance Workflow — Incident Reporting
Steps 7, 10, and 12 of the AI governance workflow, combined with the AI Governance Team escalation framework, constitute the organisation's incident detection, response, and reporting procedures under ISO 18286.6.

AI Governance Workflow — Technical Documentation
The AI governance workflow produces and retains the complete set of technical documentation required by ISO 18286.7 and Article 11, with the Step 8 conformity report serving as the primary Technical File document.

AI Governance Workflow — Record-Keeping
The AI governance workflow (Steps 2–12) generates a complete set of records at each stage, retained in the central inventory under Step 11, constituting the organisation's record-keeping system under ISO 18286.8.
